title: The sheaf condition for a finite presieve is preserved by filtered presheaf colimits
statement: Let C be a small category, Λ a small filtered category, and D : Λ → PSh(C; Sets) a diagram of presheaves of sets [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let (P, ι) be any colimit cocone of D in presheaves [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let X be an object of C and R a presieve on X with finitely many arrows (its uncurried arrow set is finite). Assume every pair of arrows in R has a pullback. If every D(i) satisfies the sheaf condition for R (every compatible family on R has a unique amalgamation), then P satisfies that same condition for R. No covering or global topology hypothesis on R is required.

source.place: Tag 0738(4), finite-stage gluing argument, applied directly to presheaf colimits and the sheaf condition of Tag 00VM; Categories Tag 002W explains finite-limit commutation. Sources read online at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0738 and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00VM.

proof.text: Evaluation of a presheaf colimit at any object is a colimit of sets, by the sectionwise presheaf colimit result. Mathlib Types.jointly_surjective_of_isColimit lifts any element to a diagram stage. For a finite family of objects and sections, choose lifts separately and a cocone over the finite discrete diagram of their stages (IsFiltered.cocone_nonempty); transport all lifts to its vertex. Naturality of the colimit coprojections preserves their images. This also works for an empty family.

An equality between two elements from the same stage holds in the filtered colimit iff some transition makes them equal (Types.FilteredColimit.isColimit_eq_iff'). For finitely many such equalities, choose their transitions and apply IsFiltered.wideSpan to obtain one transition factoring through all of them. Functoriality transports each equality along the corresponding factor. Empty families are included in wideSpan.

For separatedness, lift two candidate amalgamations over X to a common stage using Types.FilteredColimit.jointly_surjective_of_isColimit₂. Their restrictions agree in the colimit over each arrow of R. Apply finite_sections_equal, indexed by the finite uncurried arrow subtype of R, to make every equality hold at one later stage. Separatedness of that stage identifies the transported sections, and the cocone equations identify their colimit images.

For existence, lift a compatible family on R to a single stage using finite_sections_lift. Index the pairwise pullbacks by the finite square of the uncurried arrow subtype. Naturality and compatibility of the original family imply that the two restrictions over each pullback have equal colimit images. Apply finite_sections_equal to obtain one later stage where all these equations hold. Presieve.pullbackCompatible_iff makes this a compatible family there, which has an amalgamation by the assumed stagewise sheaf condition. Its image in P is an amalgamation of the original family by naturality and the cocone equations. Together with separatedness, this is the sheaf condition.

theorem finitePresieve_isSheafFor_filteredColimit
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C]
    {Λ : Type u} [SmallCategory Λ] [IsFiltered Λ]
    (D : Λ ⥤ Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (c : Cocone D) (hc : IsColimit c)
    {X : C} (R : Presieve X) [R.HasPairwisePullbacks]
    (hfinite : R.uncurry.Finite)
    (hD : ∀ i, R.IsSheafFor (D.obj i)) : R.IsSheafFor c.pt
